nounGroups.name: All topics
nounGroups.articleTip: Article counts show patterns in this word bank, not a rule for guessing new nouns. Learn each noun with its article and plural.

nounGroups.name: People & family
nounGroups.articleTip: Family words often follow a person's gender (der Vater, die Mutter), but das Kind is neuter. Learn the article with the whole noun.

nounGroups.name: Home
nounGroups.articleTip: Room and furniture words use all three genders. Meaning alone does not tell you an object's article.

nounGroups.name: Places & town
nounGroups.articleTip: Place words are mixed. Some endings offer clues, such as -straße being feminine, but learn each place word with its article.

nounGroups.name: Work
nounGroups.articleTip: Many feminine job titles use -in (die Lehrerin). Learn both forms of a profession with their articles.

nounGroups.name: School & learning
nounGroups.articleTip: Nouns ending in -ung are feminine (die Übung). Common words such as das Buch and der Stift show why endings are only clues.

nounGroups.name: Food & drink
nounGroups.articleTip: Food words are mixed: das Wasser, das Brot, der Kaffee, die Milch. Memorize the article as part of each word.

nounGroups.name: Time
nounGroups.articleTip: Time words use all three genders: der Tag, die Woche, das Jahr. Practise the article whenever you say a new time word.

nounGroups.name: Travel
nounGroups.articleTip: Travel words are mixed: der Zug, die Reise, das Fahrrad. Articles also change after many prepositions.

nounGroups.name: Health & body
nounGroups.articleTip: Body and health words are mixed. The ending -heit is a reliable feminine clue, as in die Gesundheit.

nounGroups.name: Shopping & clothing
nounGroups.articleTip: Clothing words use all three genders: das Kleid, der Schuh, die Farbe. Learn plurals for shopping situations.

nounGroups.name: Nature & weather
nounGroups.articleTip: Nature words are mixed: das Wetter, die Sonne, der Regen. Learn them in useful phrases as well as on their own.

nounGroups.name: Communication & media
nounGroups.articleTip: In a compound noun, the final noun determines gender: das Wörterbuch is neuter because Buch is neuter.

nounGroups.name: Technology & devices
nounGroups.articleTip: Borrowed device names have no dependable gender pattern. Learn each new word with its article and plural.

nounGroups.name: Public services & documents
nounGroups.articleTip: Nouns ending in -ung are feminine (die Anmeldung, die Bescheinigung). Das Formular is a useful exception to memorize.

nounGroups.name: Health & care
nounGroups.articleTip: Endings -heit and -keit are feminine (die Krankheit, die Möglichkeit). Other health terms have mixed genders.

nounGroups.name: Feelings & relationships
nounGroups.articleTip: Many abstract nouns ending in -ung or -schaft are feminine. Common words such as der Ärger still need to be learned individually.

nounGroups.name: Leisure & arts
nounGroups.articleTip: Art and leisure words are mixed. For compounds, look at the last noun: das Theaterstück follows das Stück.

nounGroups.name: Sports & movement
nounGroups.articleTip: Activity nouns formed with -en are often neuter (das Schwimmen). Equipment and sport names vary, so check each article.

nounGroups.name: Nature & landscape
nounGroups.articleTip: Landscape words are mixed: der Berg, die Insel, das Tal. Learn every new place word with its article.

nounGroups.name: Environment & weather
nounGroups.articleTip: Nouns ending in -ung are feminine (die Verschmutzung). Other environment words use mixed genders.

nounGroups.name: Travel & transport
nounGroups.articleTip: Transport nouns are mixed: der Verkehr, die Fähre, das Schiff. Learn article and plural before using a noun after a preposition.

nounGroups.name: Food & cooking
nounGroups.articleTip: Ingredients and kitchen words use all three genders. Practise each noun as a set: article, singular, plural.

nounGroups.name: Shopping & money
nounGroups.articleTip: Shopping words are mixed. Many nouns ending in -ung are feminine, such as die Überweisung.

nounGroups.name: School & language
nounGroups.articleTip: Nouns ending in -ung are feminine (die Bedeutung). Core words such as das Wort and der Satz are useful exceptions to know.

nounGroups.name: Clothing & personal care
nounGroups.articleTip: Clothing nouns do not follow one gender pattern. Learn the article and plural, then use them in phrases such as mit dem Mantel.

nounGroups.name: Household & tools
nounGroups.articleTip: Household objects use mixed genders. The article stays part of the word you memorize, even when the object seems familiar.
